author: shurjenw
body: This issue is about how to curate a binding MF term from publication for standard GO annotations. PMID: 8621665 shows that flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) binds covalently to Dmgdh.  Should the annotation to Dmgdh be flavin adenine dinucleotide binding (GO:0050660), protein flavinylation (GO:0017013) or none of them?
title: flavin adenine dinucleotide binding (GO:0050660) annotation to covalently flavinylated Dmgdh

author: ValWood
body:
Hi @shurjenw 

This is a great question. I have been trying to figure out how to model this (I realise this question is for basic GO annotation, but it was the same thought process for GO-CAM).

The annotations shouldn't be flavin adenine dinucleotide binding (GO:0050660), although often this   annotation is made automatically for many target proteins. Some flavinated proteins aren't covalent, so somtimes it is correct.

protein flavinylation (GO:0017013)  is also incorrect -this term will likely be obsoleted because 
a) it  represents an activity rather than a process, 
b)  the upstream pathway is FAD biosynthesis.  
c) In most  (but not all) covalent flavoproteins, no dedicated enzyme is required. As the polypeptide folds, it creates an active-site environment and positions the FAD.

So my take is that we would not capture this as a GO process. Instead, I would capture the targets  of the FAD biosynthesis pathway  to obtain the 'causal' links e.g.:

http://noctua.geneontology.org/workbench/noctua-visual-pathway-editor/?model_id=gomodel%3A67c10cc400001835

My question  on this issue is which relation to use  in  a GO_CAM in this and simialr situations.  Here I have temporarily modelled the FAD as an input of the target protein. I'm not sure if this is correct.

If you do want to capture the covalent flavination, the only way to do this  is to request a PRO modification term  for the Flavinated form of the protein here https://github.com/PROconsortium/PRoteinOntology/issues
I will probably do this at some point to model the flavinated forms for completeness, but first  I  need to figure out  which are binding, and which are covalent.

Does that help?

@pgaudet  can this move over to the new annotation query tracker?  I tried but can't migrate it.

author: ValWood
body:
A list. It turns out that most I could find appear to be non-covalent according to CHAT-GPT

| Protein / Enzyme | Organism (example) | Flavin cofactor | Covalently bound? | Function |
|-----------------|------------------|----------------|-----------------|---------|
| Succinate dehydrogenase (Sdh1) | Eukaryotes, bacteria | FAD | ~No~ often covalently bound to FAD via His-attachment. | TCA cycle; electron transfer to ETC |
| Acyl-CoA dehydrogenase | Eukaryotes, bacteria | FAD | No | Fatty acid β-oxidation |
| Glutathione reductase | Eukaryotes, bacteria | FAD | No | Redox homeostasis (GSSG → GSH) |
| Monoamine oxidase (MAO A/B) | Mammals | FAD | Yes | Oxidative deamination of amines |
| Lipoamide dehydrogenase | Eukaryotes, bacteria | FAD | Yes | Component of pyruvate & α-KG dehydrogenase complexes |
| NADPH–cytochrome P450 reductase | Eukaryotes | FAD, FMN | No | Electron transfer to P450 enzymes |
| Old yellow enzyme (OYE family) | Yeast, plants, bacteria | FMN | No | Reduction of α,β-unsaturated carbonyls |
| Proline dehydrogenase (Put1/PutA) | Eukaryotes, bacteria | FAD | No | Oxidation of proline to Δ¹-pyrroline-5-carboxylate |
| Sarcosine oxidase | Bacteria | FAD | Yes | Oxidation of sarcosine |
| Electron transfer flavoprotein (ETF) | Eukaryotes, bacteria | FAD | No | Shuttles electrons from dehydrogenases to respiratory chain |
| tRNA/mRNA dihydrouridine synthase (DUS1–DUS4) | Eukaryotes (yeast, human) | FAD | No | Reduction of uridine to dihydrouridine in tRNA/mRNA |
| Ferric iron reductase (FRE family) | Yeast, bacteria | FAD | No | Reduces Fe³⁺ to Fe²⁺ for iron uptake |
| Methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) | Humans, bacteria | FAD | No | Reduces 5,10-methylene-THF to 5-methyl-THF |
| Xanthine oxidase / dehydrogenase | Mammals, bacteria | FAD, Mo-cofactor | No | Purine degradation (xanthine → uric acid) |
| NADH dehydrogenase (Complex I) | Eukaryotes, bacteria | FMN | No | Electron transfer from NADH to ubiquinone |
| Pyridoxamine 5'-phosphate oxidase | Eukaryotes | FMN | No | Vitamin B6 metabolism |
| Sulfite reductase (NADPH-dependent) | Bacteria, plants | FAD | No | Reduces sulfite to sulfide using NADPH |
| Sulfide-quinone oxidoreductase (SQR) | Bacteria, mitochondria | FAD | No | Oxidizes sulfide and transfers electrons to quinones |
| Squalene monooxygenase (SQLE) | Eukaryotes | FAD | No | Converts squalene to 2,3-oxidosqualene in sterol biosynthesis |
| Protoporphyrinogen oxidase (PPOX) | Eukaryotes, bacteria | FAD | No | Oxidizes protoporphyrinogen IX to protoporphyrin IX |
| Ornithine N⁵-monooxygenase (SidA) | Fungi, bacteria | FAD | No | Hydroxylates L-ornithine at N⁵; siderophore biosynthesis |
| Nitric oxide dioxygenase | Bacteria, mammals | FAD | No | Converts NO + O₂ → nitrate (detoxification) |
| tRNA uridine 5-carboxymethylaminomethyl modification enzyme | Eukaryotes, bacteria | FAD | No | Catalyzes post-transcriptional modification of tRNA uridine |
| 2-Octaprenyl-6-methoxyphenol hydroxylase | Bacteria | FAD | No | Hydroxylation in ubiquinone biosynthesis |
| Acetolactate synthase (flavin-containing form) | Bacteria, plants | FAD | No | Catalyzes acetolactate formation in branched-chain amino acid biosynthesis |
| ER flavin-containing N,N-dimethylaniline monooxygenase (FMO) | Mammals | FAD | No | Oxygenates nucleophilic heteroatoms; xenobiotic metabolism |
| ER protein folding oxidoreductin (Ero1) | Eukaryotes | FAD | No | Catalyzes disulfide bond formation in ER protein folding |
| Glutamate synthase (GOGAT, Glt1) | Bacteria, yeast, plants | FAD | No | Converts glutamine + α-ketoglutarate → 2 glutamate in nitrogen assimilation |
| FAP1 (L-pipecolate oxidase) | Fungi, bacteria | FAD | No | Oxidizes L-pipecolate in lysine catabolism |
| FAP2 (L-saccharopine oxidase) | Fungi, bacteria | FAD | No | Oxidizes L-saccharopine in lysine degradation |
| Methionine synthase reductase (MSR) | Humans, bacteria | FAD | No | Reduces cobalamin in methionine synthase; regenerates active enzyme |


Covalent flavins: Only MAO A/B and sarcosine oxidase. + mitochondrial dihydrolipoamide dehydrogenase (e3 component of oxoglutarate dehydrogenase complex) 

Non-covalent FAD/ FMN: All others.

author: pgaudet
body:
@shurjenw 

GO binding terms should not be used to capture covalent binding. See definition of 'GO:0005488 binding': 
> The selective, non-covalent, often stoichiometric, interaction of a molecule with one or more specific sites on another molecule.

It would be possible to capture the flavin transferase activity, but that would be for the flavin transferase enzyme, and Dmgdh would be the input. Do you know which protein makes that modification ? 

Thanks, Pascale

author: ValWood
body:
